title: Productivity and quality of forage
text:
Productivity and quality of forage:

Dry matter yield (t/ha/yr), grown at the different soil fertility levels | Grasses | Legumes
Low soil fertility | 10 – 15 | 3 - 5
Medium soil fertility | 15 – 30 | 5 - 10
High soil fertility | 30 – 50 | 10 – 15
% Crude Protein (CP) | 5 – 15 | 15 – 25
% Calcium (Ca) | 0.2 - 0.5 | 0.8 - 1.9

Weed control:
- Weeds compete crops. Some are toxic to animals; some are unpalatable and injurious to grazing livestock because of thorns/spines.

Common weeds in tropical pastures:
1. Hagonoy (Chromolaena odorata)
2. Kanding-kanding (Lantana camara)
3. Talong gubat (Solanum ferox)
4. Bracken fern (Ptredium aquilinum)

Other application of forages:
1. As hedgegrows in alley cropping
2. As bounderies
3. As living fence
4. For weed control
5. Erosion control
6. Use as firewood
7. Mitigation measure for global warming

Forages utilized as a living fence (left) and boundaries (right).

facts: Under low soil fertility, grasses yield 10–15 t/ha/yr of dry matter.
Under low soil fertility, legumes yield 3–5 t/ha/yr of dry matter.
Under medium soil fertility, grasses yield 15–30 t/ha/yr of dry matter.
Under medium soil fertility, legumes yield 5–10 t/ha/yr of dry matter.
Under high soil fertility, grasses yield 30–50 t/ha/yr of dry matter.
Under high soil fertility, legumes yield 10–15 t/ha/yr of dry matter.
Weeds compete with crops; some are toxic to animals, while others are unpalatable and injurious to grazing livestock due to thorns/spines.
Hagonoy is the common name for Chromolaena odorata.
Kanding-kanding is the common name for Lantana camara.
Talong gubat is the common name for Solanum ferox.
Bracken fern is the common name for Ptredium aquilinum (Pteridium aquilinum).
Other applications of forages include: as hedgerows in alley cropping, as boundaries, as living fences, for weed control, erosion control, firewood, and as a mitigation measure for global warming.
